extracted.intended_audience: investigative journalists, journalism educators, students, newsroom leaders, and prospective IRE members
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of Investigative Reporters & Editors' mission, core values, programs, diversity/inclusion commitments, code of conduct, and program expectations for members and fellows. Intended to guide organizational behavior, programming, and member expectations within investigative journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing training, resources, and a community of support to investigative journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: IRE accomplishes its mission by providing training, resources, and a community of support to investigative journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes access to thousands of reporting tipsheets and materials via the Resource Center, conferences, specialized training nationwide, and programs such as NICAR that offer data journalism resources and instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting high professional standards
rubrics_metrics.description: IRE commits to promoting high professional standards in investigative journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a core mission pillar; manifests in training, conferences, ethics guidance, and governance designed to uphold journalistic quality and integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting the rights of investigative journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: IRE seeks to protect the rights of investigative journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied activities include advocacy, legal/rights resources, and organizational support when journalists face threats to reporting or safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring the future of IRE
rubrics_metrics.description: IRE works to ensure its organizational continuity and capacity to serve members into the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers governance, fundraising choices (e.g., reliance on professional organizations and journalists rather than non-journalistic foundations historically), board oversight, and programs to sustain membership and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen democracy by empowering a resilient, inclusive community
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board envisions IRE strengthening democracy by empowering a resilient, inclusive and forward-looking community of investigative journalists to uncover truths and serve the public good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This vision frames organizational priorities, including training, advocacy, inclusivity, and supporting journalism that serves the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize working well together with IRE staff and members; contribute to collective goals and be active, informed, and respectful participants in decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board and member conduct should emphasize cooperative decision-making and respect for contributors' roles and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a broad range of voices, backgrounds, abilities and communities represented on the Board; actively ensure everyone can speak and be heard; foster open, inclusive dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board explicitly centers representation and equitable participation as a guiding value for governance and programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Act thoughtfully and effectively, make timely, streamlined and mission-focused decisions, and demonstrate respect for the work and roles of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-making should be mission-focused and avoid unnecessary delay or bureaucracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct business openly; follow well-executed governance policies; be accountable to members and set an example for the journalism industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes sharing legal documents, meeting minutes, and clear governance practices to maintain accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead with conviction, driven by journalists’ responsibility to inform the public, and be willing to innovate, evolve and take risks necessary to move IRE and its membership into the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports willingness to adopt new programs, advocate on sensitive issues, and take principled stands in service of public-interest journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect diversity and inclusion in all efforts and offerings (D&I mission)
rubrics_metrics.description: IRE strives to reflect diversity and inclusion in all of its efforts and offerings as a foundational value that strengthens the organization and produces higher-quality journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, this means centering inclusivity in public programming and internal staffing, creating safe spaces for marginalized journalists, and ensuring programming accessibility across identities and backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain necessary data collection to support D&I commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: IRE will maintain the necessary data collection to assure membership of its commitment to diversity and inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: collecting racial and gender makeup of membership and awards entrants; reporting percentages (e.g., at least 30% membership identified as POC in recent data) and using these data to guide improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and maintain discrimination-free, supportive environments
rubrics_metrics.description: IRE seeks to maintain a discrimination-free organization where everyone can learn and be supported professionally — including at conferences and events held in states with evolving laws and legal protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program design and event policies should consider legal/regulatory contexts and proactively protect participant safety and inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct: provide a friendly, safe, and welcoming environment
rubrics_metrics.description: IRE is committed to providing a friendly, safe and welcoming environment for all, regardless of race, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, sexual orientation, physical ability, age, appearance, or religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports vigorous debate but requires civil and respectful behavior. Discriminatory or harassing behavior is prohibited and IRE may take actions including exclusion from events, forums, listservs, and the organization itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility-first conference design (AccessFest)
rubrics_metrics.description: AccessFest is a virtual-by-design conference aimed to provide investigative and data training at lower cost and with accessibility in mind for health, caregiving, and financial constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference planning should prioritize virtual access, affordable participation, and content that allows deeper engagement on diversity/belonging/equity/inclusion topics; selection of diverse keynote speakers is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center diversity, belonging, equity, and inclusion (DBEI) in programming
rubrics_metrics.description: AccessFest and related programming center DBEI both in news coverage and within the newsroom, offering deeper sessions than general conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming should enable journalists to investigate inequality in communities and help newsrooms address diversity-related challenges; keynote and session curation should prioritize historically marginalized perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: NICAR program pillars for data journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: NICAR shares IRE’s mission to foster excellence, particularly in data journalism, by making government datasets available, doing custom analysis, holding conferences, training journalists in data skills, providing resources for responsible data use, and training students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NICAR's services constitute standards for quality data journalism: access to datasets, technical training (acquiring, cleaning, analyzing data), ethical/responsible use of data, and capacity-building through conferences and community support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chauncey Bailey Journalist of Color Investigative Reporting Fellowship structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The yearlong fellowship provides immersive IRE training, resources and a mentor network; fellows remain in their newsroom and produce an investigative story/package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship expectations include in-newsroom reporting with mentorship and resources; program funded by donors and partner organizations; named in honor of Chauncey Bailey.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRE on Campus program goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides investigative and data training for journalism educators and students with special opportunities for HBCUs, HSIs, and Minority-Serving Institutions, plus data journalism bootcamps and fellowships to cover costs for educators of color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program design aims to expand training access to underrepresented institutions and educators, include hands-on skills training, and offer financial support mechanisms to increase participation and capacity-building.
